products.note: Verified in the research for The AI Ready School. AI: Leveled texts, quizzes. Use: Leveled news and content at five reading levels. Who: Teachers, students. Student age: Under 13 only through a student account provided by a teacher, parent, or administrator. reading.body:
Newsela raised $21.0 million across two Form D filings in 2014 and 2015, and its only tracked product is an education AI platform sold to schools rather than to data centers.

The two filings are small and old. The 2014 round sold $5,956,174 against an identical offering, and the 2015 round sold $14,999,966 of a $15,500,001 offering, with first sales in May 2015 and the filing in October. Both are unamended originals, so they record what was sold at filing time, not the final close. Nothing in the data shows later raises, valuation, revenue, or headcount.

What the company sells is leveled text and quizzes at five reading levels, plus an AI teaching assistant for lesson planning and text differentiation. Its distribution runs through teachers, schools, and districts, with under-13 students admitted only through an account a teacher, parent, or administrator provides, and privacy terms registered with the Student Data Privacy Consortium in New York. Pricing is free at a limited tier and on request for districts.

For AI scaling, this is the demand side that does not touch the binding constraint. A product like this consumes inference and storage, not gigawatts, and its growth is gated by school budgets and procurement cycles rather than by interconnection queues or turbine supply. The data cannot say how much compute Newsela buys, where it is hosted, or whether its AI features run on third-party models, so no claim about its power footprint follows from these filings.

profile_text.body:
Newsela is a content and assessment platform for schools, which the company describes as aligned to national and state standards and flexible enough to support relevant curriculum. The site says it helps teachers find content for lessons and offers AI-powered tools intended to simplify daily instruction, including an AI-powered teaching assistant for lesson planning, activity design, graphic organizer creation, and text differentiation.

Its tracked product is also named Newsela, listed under education and research AI. It provides leveled texts and quizzes, with leveled news and content at five reading levels, for teachers and students. Students under 13 use it only through a student account provided by a teacher, parent, or administrator. Signed agreements appear in the Student Data Privacy Consortium registry (Erie 1 BOCES, New York). Newsela Lite is free with limited content, and district pricing is available on request.
